title: AI-Run Modern LaTeX Manuscript Workflow and Replication Packet
description:
Compact workflow and replication record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. It documents the AI-run scan-to-TeX-to-translation-to-audit-to-publication workflow, including local source acquisition, OCR/math-OCR witness generation, source-image slicing, high-DPI object crops, TeX compilation, web review handoffs, GitHub mirroring, and Zenodo publication.

Latest workflow status, 2026-07-03. The public workflow now distinguishes source-support, live ledger, active gap-pass, compact promoted delta, reader release, and critical edition. Noether R685/R686 are no-patch source-support/direct-audit layers; R687 is a narrow P40 p537 TeX-changing source repair; R688 is a narrow P24 p234 norm-separator repair; R690 is a narrow P13 source-merge package promoting seven verified fixes, not corpus closure. SGA5 p480 is a local French body-workpass ledger claim for a selected 10-exposé branch, with about 60 numbered TeX-fix events and ERRATA 115, not English synchronization, global source-faithfulness, or critical-edition closure. Weber Volume I p1-p76 is an active source gap-pass with about 75 fix events, not a new reader release. GitHub and Zenodo metadata should preserve these object classes instead of collapsing them into completion claims.

Archive scope guardrail. Local sweep may inspect broad folders, but publication is limited to the manuscript transcription/translation/source-audit project unless Floris explicitly requests a named non-project upload. A file being mathematical, interesting, recently downloaded, or technically publishable is not enough.

Witness and locator rule. OCR, VLM, detector, crop, candidate-TeX, derivative PDF, failed web-run transcript, source-inventory output, validation sidecar, and first-page visual-triage contact sheet are witness and locator layers unless a source-specific audit promotes them. Source scans and source-object witnesses remain authority for transcription claims. Agent and swarm passes are finders rather than certifiers.

Useful current lessons. The SGA5 and Weber lanes show that compact promoted deltas can lag behind local workpass ledgers; public text must say which is which. SGA recert spot-checks found defects after a local completion claim, and Weber p1-p76 shows compile-clean pages can still omit displays, cross-references, and intermediate calculations. The Weber sample-cert failure shows that compile-clean, mathematically related TeX can still fail as transcription. The Noether R564 reversal and R687/R688 promotions show that source witnesses govern both promotion and rejection. The laptop Noether language-planning branch is useful as a source of sidecars and interlanguage logs, but whole-branch merges can downgrade current archive docs; inspect subtrees and import selectively.

Companion records. Interlanguage and constructed-language methodology lives at 10.5281/zenodo.21124403. Lean 4 / Mathlib-style formalization sidecars live at 10.5281/zenodo.21129946. These are useful methodology/formalization lanes, not source-fidelity certification, translation certification, page-completeness certification, or critical editions.

Corrections and contributions. Workflow corrections, tool notes, reproducibility improvements, and issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
version: 2026-07-03 object-class caveat refresh: SGA recert, Weber fix75, Noether R690
notes: July 3 workflow refresh: no-patch source-support, live ledger/workpass cursors, active gap-passes, and narrow source-merge packages must remain distinct from compact promoted deltas, reader releases, critical editions, and source-certification claims. R690, SGA5 p480 recert, and Weber p76/fix75 are status/control evidence, not completion claims.
